court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: Additional District Judge (Matrimonial Cases) Jammu, CR No. 31/2008(O&M)
facts_of_case: Petitioner's husband absented himself from proceedings; petitioner filed application for grant of interim maintenance under section 30 of the Hindu Marriage Act; trial court set aside ex parte order and granted maintenance pendente lite as well as litigation expenses

legal_principles.principle: The provisions of the Limitation Act are applicable when a remedy is availed under the Code of Civil Procedure.
legal_principles.held: It has been submitted that the provisions of the Limitation Act are applicable when the applicant avails the remedy under the Code of Civil Procedure and as such, there is no illegality in the order impugned.

legal_principles.principle: When a decree is passed ex-parte, the respondent can resort to the provisions contained in the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex-parte decree/order.
legal_principles.held: As per section 23 of Jammu and Kashmir Hindu Marriage Act, the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure have been made applicable to the proceedings under the Hindu Marriage Act so far as the same are not inconsistent with the provisions of the Jammu and Kashmir Hindu Marriage Act.
applicable_acts_sections: Jammu and Kashmir Hindu Marriage Act — Section 23

outcome.final_order: Order dated 28.11.2007 set aside by the High Court

use_for_drafting: preparing appeals against ex parte orders
